editorial.body.old_excerpt: Retail rice is a more precise activity than its plain title suggests. It covers the specia
editorial.body.new:
Retail rice is a more precise activity than its plain title suggests. It covers the specialised retail sale of a range of rice varieties, including Cianjur, Cisadane, Saigon and glutinous rice. The focus is not merely rice as a commodity, but its sale through a retail activity dedicated to the category and its distinct varieties. That specificity gives the activity a clear commercial identity: a business built around retailing rice in its many recognised forms.

Nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling for this activity is 0%. Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II p.13-14, entry 46, sub-row "Beras" (ex-KBLI 2020 47241) allocates retail of rice (beras) as a specialised store to Koperasi and UMKM (the *dialokasikan* column), so a PT PMA cannot register it anywhere in Indonesia — not only in Bali.

editorial.body.old_excerpt: **This is a retail activity defined by processed meat.** The scope is specialised retail s
editorial.body.new:
**This is a retail activity defined by processed meat.** The scope is specialised retail sale of varied processed-meat products, not a broad food-trade label. Its examples—sausages, bakso meatballs, and abon, a shredded-meat preparation—make the commercial centre of gravity clear: the sale of meat that has already been prepared or processed. The scope spans products made from beef, pork, poultry, lamb, rabbit, goat and camel, as well as other fresh meats named in the record. The record presents a retail activity whose identity comes from the processed nature of its merchandise. That specificity keeps the registration anchored to a particular retail offer rather than to meat in general.

**The scale range is broad.** The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. That is the whole stated scale spectrum, so it is not presented as a narrow category available only to one business size. The scope remains specialised retail of processed-meat products of the kinds described in the record. For operators, this produces a clear description: a specialty retail business centred on processed-meat goods. The four scale labels set out the stated business-size range; they do not broaden the activity into meat commerce generally. Its boundaries remain merchandise-led and retail-specific.

Nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling for this activity is 0%. Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II p.13-14, entry 46, sub-row "Daging dan ikan olahan" (ex-KBLI 2020 47245 — split heir, together with 47246, of the one row naming both meat and fish) allocates retail of processed meat (daging olahan) as a specialised store to Koperasi and UMKM (the *dialokasikan* column), so a PT PMA cannot register it anywhere in Indonesia — not only in Bali.

editorial.body.new:
This activity is the retail sale of processed fish, shrimp and shellfish products. Its scope includes salted or dried seafood, alongside products such as fish sausage, fish balls and shredded fish. The examples range across anchovy, shark, scad, grouper and other fish, as well as shrimp, tiny shrimp, squid, clams, mussels and shellfish. The classification is deliberately broad in its retail setting: it covers sales conducted inside a building as well as relevant trade from roadside stalls, shop-front verandas, and movable or pushable market stalls.

That breadth matters because the activity describes the point of sale, not a single product format or a single retail environment. A business may register it for the retail trade of varied processed seafood products, whether the offering is anchored in dried and salted goods or in processed forms such as sausage, fish balls and shredded fish. It is open across the full listed scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The record therefore gives the activity room to serve small retail operations and larger businesses within the same classification.

Nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling for this activity is 0%. Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II p.13-14, entry 46, sub-row "Daging dan ikan olahan" (ex-KBLI 2020 47245 — split heir, together with 47245, of the one row naming both meat and fish) allocates retail of processed fish (ikan olahan) as a specialised store to Koperasi and UMKM (the *dialokasikan* column), so a PT PMA cannot register it anywhere in Indonesia — not only in Bali.

editorial.body.old_excerpt: This activity is the retail trade of pharmaceutical preparations for human use outside a c
editorial.body.new:
This activity is the retail trade of pharmaceutical preparations for human use outside a conventional pharmacy setting. Its scope is broad in form rather than in medical purpose: tablets, capsules, ointments, solutions, parenteral solutions and suspensions all sit within it. The record specifically includes products associated with skin, eye, dental, ear, respiratory, digestive, blood-pressure and hormonal conditions, alongside vitamins and health supplements. In practice, it reaches drug stores, Type B village pharmacies and pharmaceutical market stalls, as well as mobile and internet-based medicine sales.

The activity is open across the full stated scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed as a niche format reserved for a single kind of outlet. It accommodates a fixed retail presence, market-based selling, circulation through mobile sales, and an online channel. The common thread is the retail sale of pharmaceutical preparations for people; the setting may change, but the activity remains defined by that retail function.

Nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling for this activity is 0%. Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II p.13-14, entry 46, sub-row "Barang dan obat farmasi untuk manusia bukan di apotik" (ex-KBLI 2020 47722) allocates retail of non-prescription pharmaceutical goods outside a pharmacy (Toko Obat) as a specialised store to Koperasi and UMKM (the *dialokasikan* column), so a PT PMA cannot register it anywhere in Indonesia — not only in Bali.
